@graph.articleBody: If you searched for "Google Guaranteed," you probably saw a green check on a competitor's listing and wondered how to get one. Here is the first thing to know: the program still exists, but the name changed. Google's current help pages call the badge Google Verified. "Google Guaranteed" is the old name, and it is still how most people search for it, which is why so many articles online mix the two. This guide is only about the badge: what it signals to customers, how a business earns it, why some businesses cannot get it, and what you can do to prepare. mainEntity.name: Is Google Guaranteed still a thing?

acceptedAnswer.text: The name is old. Google's current help pages call the badge Google Verified and do not use "Google Guaranteed." People still search for the old name, so you will see it in older articles.

mainEntity.name: What does the Google Verified badge mean?

acceptedAnswer.text: It signals that your business passed Google's screening process. Provider profiles display the badge along with the specific verification checks the business completed.

mainEntity.name: What does Google check before giving the badge?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google says the screening procedures vary by category and region and may include license, insurance and background checks. Whenever applicable, each business must be insured, and the insurance type and minimum amount depend on the category and location.

mainEntity.name: Which businesses cannot get the badge?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google says the badge is currently unavailable for the auto, beauty and dining categories. For other trades, availability depends on category and region, so check the sign-up flow for your trade and city.

mainEntity.name: Can I get the badge without Local Services Ads?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google's pages describe the badge as part of Local Services Ads. They do not describe a way to get it outside that program.

mainEntity.name: Does the badge guarantee a better ad ranking?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Google's pages do not say that. They say your ad ranking may be affected if you regularly fail to answer calls or respond to messages.
